title: "SAE Toolkit"
subtitle: "Bring your own survey into the workflow"
number-sections: false
---

This SAE toolkit shows how to adapt the tutorial workflow to your own survey, geography, and outcome by mapping your data to a common schema and applying reusable scripts.

## 1. Define the estimates you need

Start by defining the estimand that covers:

- what outcome is being estimated;
- who is in the target population;
- at which spatial scale;
- over which time periods.

In a spatio-temporal SAE workflow, the target estimate is produced for every area-by-period combination. This tutorial calls that combination an **area-time cell**.

## 2. Prepare the input tables

The workflow expects a set of datasets, linked by `area_id` and `time_id` values, with `unit_id` as the survey respondent identifier.

### Domain frame

One row for every area-time cell that should receive an estimate. This table defines the target grid, including cells with no survey respondents.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area to estimate |
| `time_id` | Time period to estimate |
| labels | Optional area or period labels |

### Survey indicator

One row per respondent-period for the outcome being estimated, together with the unit-level predictors.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unit_id` | Respondent identifier |
| `area_id` | Area assigned to the respondent |
| `time_id` | Survey period |
| `indicator` | Outcome used in estimation (binary or continuous) |
| `weight` | Survey design weight |
| `strata` | Survey stratum, if available |
| predictors | Unit predictors (age, sex, car access, etc.) |

### Area predictors

One row per area, with predictors used to explain spatial differences in the outcome. These are used in area-level SAE and can also support unit-level SAE, when they provide the area-level summaries to aggregate predictions.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area identifier |
| `scaled_*` | Predictors transformed for modelling |
| `raw_*` | Predictors in original units for interpretation and aggregation |

### Poststratification table

Used when model predictions are aggregated over population groups to produce the final estimate in the Multilevel Regression with Poststratification (MRP) workflow.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area identifier |
| `time_id` | Time period |
| population groups | Age, sex, household type, or other poststratification categories |
| `pop_count` | Population count for each cell |

## 5. Expected outputs

All method outputs should keep the same identifying columns so estimates can be compared, mapped, and joined back to other urban datasets.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Estimated area |
| `time_id` | Estimated period |
| `estimate` | Direct or model-based point estimate |
| `variance` | Sampling or posterior variance |
| `lower`, `upper` | Uncertainty interval bounds |
| `n` | Sample size |
| `method` | Direct, Fay--Herriot, etc. |
| remark | Model specification or other notes |
